drhp.business: The Company manufactures and sells speciality cotton yarn and knitted fabrics — core textile products that serve as essential inputs to the global apparel and textile industry. Production runs across five units of compact spinning and knitting facilities at Kanniyapuram and Dindigul in Tamil Nadu, supported by captive wind and rooftop-solar power. Customers are garment manufacturers who buy the Company's cotton yarn and knitted fabrics, and exports make up the large majority of turnover.

litigation.note: Three disclosed matters. (1) BRSR Principle 1 fines: BSE and NSE levied a fine for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1)(b) and 17(1A) of SEBI (LODR) 2015 consequent to the exchanges' interpretation of those regulations; the Company paid the fine and, after NSE rejected the waiver application, the matter is contested in SAT and pending disposal. (2) Contingent liabilities note: GST demands for FY2017-18, FY2018-19 and FY2019-20 relating to non-reversal of input tax credit and GST on free supply of canteen service to employees, with an appeal filed before the GSTAT; the Company is advised the demand is not sustainable in law and no provision is considered. (3) Income-tax demand for AY 2024-25 following disallowances in an assessment under section 143(3), appealed before the NFAC, again with no provision considered. A customs-duty claim disclosed in the prior year was disposed of by the Commissioner (Appeals) CGST & Central Excise in the Company's favour, so no demand subsists.

risks.note: Raw cotton is the main input and, being an agricultural produce, its price is subject to fluctuation and to government policies; the BRSR material-issues table logs it as both a risk and an opportunity. The Company's stated mitigation is purchasing across markets and settling contracts without any renegotiation. MD&A lists 'Stability in Raw cotton prices' among its risks and concerns, and raw cotton is the single largest line within materials consumed.
risks.risk: Raw cotton price and availability — single dominant agricultural input

risks.note: Exports accounted for 72.90% of total turnover (inclusive of SEZ sales) against 72.43% in the previous year, served across 9 countries. Geographically, Asia is by far the largest destination in the geographical segment disclosure. Demand patterns, tariff actions, logistics costs and geopolitical tension therefore transmit almost directly to revenue, and management states that actual growth during the year was impacted by continued geopolitical disruptions and global market uncertainties.
risks.risk: Export concentration — roughly three-quarters of turnover is exported

risks.note: Sale revenue to two customers amounting to Rs. 30629.80 Lakhs each exceeded 10% of the Company's sale revenue (previous year three customers, Rs. 33380 Lakhs). Loss or reduced offtake from either would be material, though the Company notes customers are long-standing, high-credit-quality entities in the top quartile of the value chain.
risks.risk: Customer concentration — two customers each above 10% of revenue

risks.note: Management states the substantial operations of the Company are exports and imports and are subject to foreign-currency fluctuation risk, mitigated by foreign-currency forward contracts on underlying exposures plus a natural hedge from exports exceeding imports. The disclosed sensitivity is that a 5% move in the currency rate affects profit by Rs. 284.58 Lakhs either way as at 31.03.2026, and the net foreign-currency exposure is a liability position.
risks.risk: Foreign-currency fluctuation on substantial export and import flows

risks.note: Manufacture of cotton yarn is energy based, logged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk/opportunity mitigated by 27.4 MW of windmills and 8.33 MW of rooftop solar. risks.risk: Energy intensity and dependence on wind/solar generation conditions

currentContext.expansion: The Company operates five units of compact spinning and knitting capacity at Kanniyapuram and Dindigul in Tamil Nadu, with windmills at Tirunelveli, Dharapuram and Theni; BRSR Section A counts 5 plants and 2 offices, all in India. During FY 2025-26 the Company invested in capacity and infrastructure entirely from internal accruals, allocated to plant and machinery, factory building and capital work-in-progress, and established a new Stenter plant for the knitting division to heat-process fabrics; an EHT line (110 KVA sub-station) is installed to ensure smooth flow of quality power. capex_expansion.body: The Company operates five units of compact spinning and knitting capacity at Kanniyapuram and Dindigul in Tamil Nadu, with windmills at Tirunelveli, Dharapuram and Theni; BRSR Section A counts 5 plants and 2 offices, all in India. Installed compact spindle capacity rose to 114,336 spindles from 108,288 spindles in the previous year, alongside a knitting facility converting 40,000 Kgs of yarn per day into fabrics. During FY 2025-26 the Company invested in capacity and infrastructure entirely from internal accruals, allocated to plant and machinery, factory building and capital …

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Speciality compact cotton yarn positioning — 'on account of manufacturing specialty cotton yarn, continues to have good demand and has created specific markets for its products'
- Quality/product advantage from meticulous raw-material selection and proprietary in-house technology, delivering a low fall rate for downstream garment manufacturers and thereby improving customer production efficiency
- Traceability credentials: approved as a certified spinner by reputed international brands as global brands extend sourcing traceability to spinner level, backed by a broad suite of …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Raw cotton is the main input and, being an agricultural produce, its price is subject to fluctuation and to government policies; the BRSR material-issues table logs it as both a risk and an opportunity. The Company's stated mitigation is purchasing across markets and settling contracts without any renegotiation. MD&A lists 'Stability in Raw cotton prices' among its risks and concerns, and raw cotton is the single largest line within materials consumed.
- Exports accounted for 72.90% of total turnover (inclusive of SEZ sales) against 72.43% in the previous year, served across 9 countries. Geographically, Asia is by far the largest destination in the geographical segment disclosure. Demand patterns, tariff actions, logistics costs and geopolitical tension therefore transmit almost directly to revenue, and management states that actual growth during the year was impacted by continued geopolitical disruptions and global market uncertainties.
- Sale revenue to two customers amounting to Rs. 30629.80 Lakhs each exceeded 10% of the Company's sale revenue (previous year three customers, Rs. 33380 Lakhs). Loss or reduced offtake from either would be material, though the Company notes customers are long-standing, high-credit-quality entities in the top quartile of the value chain.
- Management states the substantial operations of the Company are exports and imports and are subject to foreign-currency fluctuation risk, mitigated by foreign-currency forward contracts on underlying exposures plus a natural hedge from exports exceeding imports. The disclosed sensitivity is that a 5% move in the currency rate affects profit by Rs. 284.58 Lakhs either way as at 31.03.2026, and the net foreign-currency exposure is a liability position.
- Manufacture of cotton yarn is energy based, logged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk/opportunity mitigated by 27.4 MW of windmills and 8.33 MW of rooftop solar. MD&A's risks and concerns explicitly name 'Evacuation of 100% Wind energy generated to State Grid and favorable wind season', so both grid evacuation and wind-season variability are management-flagged dependencies of the cost structure.
- Listed directly among MD&A's risks and concerns. The Directors' Report states that while quality standards were upheld, actual growth during the year was impacted by continued ongoing geopolitical disruptions and global market uncertainties, which disrupted demand patterns and supply-chain dynamics across key regions.
- MD&A names 'Increase in Cost of Interest in the recent periods' and 'Logistics of transport of imported raw materials' among risks and concerns. Working-capital borrowings are short term; management states interest-rate fluctuation would not impact profitability in terms of debt servicing, and the Company reports itself debt free with no long-term liabilities, so the exposure sits in the working-capital cycle and in import logistics rather than in leverage.
- BSE and NSE levied a fine for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1)(b) and 17(1A) of SEBI (LODR) 2015; the Company paid it and, after NSE rejected the waiver, the matter is contested in SAT and pending disposal. Separately, GST demands for FY2017-18 to FY2019-20 (non-reversal of input tax credit and GST on free canteen supply) are under appeal before the GSTAT, and an income-tax demand for AY 2024-25 is under appeal before the NFAC, with no provision made in either case.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Stay in speciality compact cotton yarn, where the Company says it continues to have good demand and has created specific markets for its products
- Widen the product range in the knitting segment, which the Company says has established newer markets and supports more sustained profitable operations
- Strengthen the production base by modernisation, adding balancing equipment and improvising the production process — a continuing, stated programme rather than a one-off
- Modernise the plant at an estimated cost of Rs. 130.00 Crores funded entirely from internal accruals, operational from March 2027 …

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

hero.oneLiner: Ambika Cotton Mills is a Coimbatore-based manufacturer of speciality compact cotton yarn and knitted fabrics for global garment makers, with exports accounting for 72.90% of total turnover.
